\chapter{Boolean Analysis --- Norms}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomVariables.Norms
\section{Overview}
Subtracting an independent centered copy increases every affine norm of exponent at least one. An independent uniform sign also dominates the corresponding affine norm with the original variable halved, including the essential-supremum endpoint.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Norm inequality under symmetrization]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.symmetrization_norm_le}
\leanok
\difficulty{6}
Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, let $X,X':\Omega\to\mathbb R$ have the same
distribution and be independent, and let $q\in[0,\infty]$ satisfy $1\le q$. Suppose
$X\in L^q(\mu)$ and $\int X\,d\mu=0$. Then for every $a\in\mathbb R$,
$\|a+X\|_{L^q(\mu)}\le\|a+X-X'\|_{L^q(\mu)}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Random-sign moment comparison]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.randomization_norm_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsRademacherRV, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsRademacherRV.map_eq}
\difficulty{6}
Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, let $X,r:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, let
$q\in[1,\infty]$, and let $a\in\mathbb R$. Suppose $X$ belongs to $L^q(\mu)$, has
integral zero, and is independent of $r$, where $r$ is a measurable Rademacher variable:
it equals $1$ or $-1$ almost everywhere and each value has probability $1/2$. Then
$\|a+X/2\|_{L^q(\mu)}\le\|a+rX\|_{L^q(\mu)}$, where these are the extended $L^q$ norms.
\end{theorem}
